newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand short end closes weaker but off lows.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand short end closes weaker but off lows.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
The short end of the New Zealand yield curve ended a quiet Thursday session weaker but off its lows while the long end remained intact.
Selling in the short end was put down to weakness on the Trade-Weighted Index, which sank at one point to a low of 67.33. By the close the TWI had regained some ground, ending at 67.42.

"I think it (the short end) needed to do some work against the TWI when the Monetary Conditions Index was out at minus 0.82. It needed to come off a little bit against the TWI, but since then the TWI has been looking reasonably solid," said one Wellington dealer.
He expected a bid tone to emerge on Friday if the TWI holds.
Long bonds escaped the selling pressure and eased in yield by a few basis points.
"I think that fundamentally there are not a lot of reasons to sell our long bonds," the dealer said.
